claim.why_it_matters: Two index entries merged on one line. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: The printed page (index p.910, PDF p934) shows at the top of the right column two separate entries on separate lines: 'EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES exception 103, 444, 474' and 'EC-RAISING exception 444'. The transcription page-934.md line 62 holds both on one source line, 'EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES exception 103, 444, 474 EC-RAISING exception 444', with no line break between them, so they render as one entry. The neighbouring entries (lines 64-67) end with a backslash hard break, so this is a real merge of two entries and not just a difference in wrapping. All page numbers are kept and stay in order, so nothing in the standard's content is lost. The merge is a structural defect in an informative index, not a normative one.
verdict.corrected_description: Index entries 'EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES exception 103, 444, 474' and 'EC-RAISING exception 444' are merged into one transcription line (page-934.md line 62) without a line break. Every page reference is still there and in order, so the only problem is that the entry boundary is unclear. The index is informative.
